answer: With a Registered domain bound by signed confirmation letter with revocation on transfer, the account is only as strong as its binding: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the signed confirmation letter is recorded, and revocation on transfer keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One tide proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. The basalt test catches the lazy fake and the sonnet test catches the patient one.
